slides.title: Introduction to System.Math
slides.content: The System.Math class provides static methods for mathematical operations. It includes rounding, powers, roots, and min/max comparisons.

exercise.prompt: Which namespace contains the Math class?

slides.title: Math.Max and Math.Min
slides.content: Math.Max returns the larger of two numbers, and Math.Min returns the smaller. Both work with int, double, decimal, and other numeric types.
slides.example:
int high = Math.Max(10, 20); // 20
int low = Math.Min(10, 20);  // 10

exercise.prompt: What method returns the smaller of two numbers?

slides.title: Math.Sqrt
slides.content: Math.Sqrt returns the square root of a number. It accepts and returns a double. Passing a negative number returns NaN.
slides.example:
double root = Math.Sqrt(49); // 7.0
double bad = Math.Sqrt(-1);   // NaN

slides.title: Math.Round
slides.content: Math.Round rounds a number to the nearest integer or specified decimal places. It uses banker's rounding by default (rounds .5 to the nearest even number).

exercise.prompt: What does Math.Round(2.5) return by default?

slides.title: Math.Pow
slides.content: Math.Pow(base, exponent) computes the value of a number raised to a power. Both parameters are doubles, and the result is a double.
slides.example:
double square = Math.Pow(5, 2); // 25
double cube = Math.Pow(3, 3);   // 27

exercise.prompt: What method computes base raised to an exponent?

slides.title: Other Math Methods
slides.content: Math.Abs returns absolute value, Math.Ceiling rounds up, Math.Floor rounds down, and Math.Truncate removes the decimal portion.

exercise.prompt: Match the method to its behavior.

slides.title: Practical Examples
slides.content: Combine Math methods to solve real problems like finding the range of a dataset, computing distance, or normalizing scores.

exercise.prompt: Which method finds the larger of two values?

slides.title: Practice: Math Class
slides.content: Use Math methods to compute statistics like max, min, square root, and power. Practice chaining methods for complex calculations.

exercise.prompt: Calculate 5 squared using Math.Pow and 25 square-rooted using Math.Sqrt. Print both results.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: Math.Pow, Math.Sqrt
When run, your code should output: 25, 5
